attempts.summary: Created an opsbot account on node1 (RHEL 7) with an ed25519 keypair, authorized that public key for opsbot on node2 (RHEL 7), and enforced key-only SSH authentication for opsbot on both nodes via a Match User opsbot sshd_config block (PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey). Implemented entirely with Ansible, run from node3 (the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed, used strictly as the control node). Since ansible-core 2.20 on node3 requires Python 3 on managed nodes but node1/node2 only have Python 2.7 with no working package repos, all target tasks use Ansible's raw module (no target-side Python dependency) instead of standard modules. Verified opsbot can SSH from node1 to node2 non-interactively with the key, and that password-preferred SSH attempts against opsbot on both nodes are rejected (Permission denied (publickey)) while sshd reports AuthenticationMethods=publickey for that user. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id/uptime/service baselines on all three nodes, rebooted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (never concurrently), confirmed each node's boot_id changed and command execution resumed, and re-verified opsbot's account, keys, sshd policy, and live node1-to-node2 SSH access after each reboot, culminating in a full successful re-run of the Ansible playbook after node3's own reboot.
